model_claims.text: The original `encode_multipart_formdata` materialized the entire encoded body in a BytesIO and copied it again, causing roughly 2N memory usage for a payload of size N.
model_claims.source_quote: `encode_multipart_formdata` materialized the entire encoded body in a `BytesIO` and copied it again with `getvalue()`, so uploading a file of size N cost roughly 2N in memory (on top of the caller's own copy).

model_claims.text: `Part` represents a single body part and mirrors `io.BufferedReader` with `read()` and `peek()` over chunks, streaming file-like data incrementally without loading it fully into memory.
model_claims.source_quote: - `Part` represents a single body part and mirrors `io.BufferedReader` with `read()` and `peek()` over chunks of the part. Part data may be bytes, str, int, or a binary file-like object; file-like data is streamed incrementally and never loaded into memory in full.

model_claims.text: `MultipartEncoder` is a readable stream over the encoded body that supports a complete rewind via `seek(0,0)`, provides `content_type` and a `length`/`__len__` for Content-Length when all part lengths are known.
model_claims.source_quote: - `MultipartEncoder` is a readable stream over the encoded body with a complete rewind via `seek(0, 0)` that attempts to rewind every body part, plus `content_type` and a `length`/`__len__` for `Content-Length` framing when all part lengths are known.

model_claims.text: `MultipartDecoder` parses a multipart body (bytes or a stream) back into `Part` objects, extracting the boundary via `from_content_type()`.
model_claims.source_quote: - `MultipartDecoder` parses a multipart body (bytes or a stream) back into `Part` objects, with `from_content_type()` boundary extraction.

model_claims.text: `encode_multipart_formdata` now uses `MultipartEncoder` internally but its output and return contract remain unchanged, verified byte-for-byte against the previous implementation.
model_claims.source_quote: `encode_multipart_formdata` now uses `MultipartEncoder` internally; its output and return contract are unchanged (verified byte-for-byte against the previous implementation by the existing tests).

model_claims.text: Streaming a 50 MiB file part in 64 KiB chunks with the new implementation peaks at only 0.25 MiB of additional allocation, whereas the old `encode_multipart_formdata` peaks at about 2× the payload size.
model_claims.source_quote: Memory verification with memray: streaming a 50 MiB file part in 64 KiB chunks peaks at 0.25 MiB of additional allocation, and a `pytest.mark.limit_memory("5 MB")` regression test streams a 32 MiB part. By comparison, the bytes-returning `encode_multipart_formdata` peaks at ~2x the payload, which is inherent to its contract.
